title: Power Rankings: Banged-up Bulls still NBA's best
heading: 2011-12 Power Rankings: Week 4
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: As long as this turf-toe deal eventually heals, Rose and the Bulls are bound to be grateful later that he's getting rest now and that they're getting away with it in the short term against a string of sub-.500 foes. Think you already know what it means if the toe isn't healing properly.

rankings.summaryHtml: Something tells me Miami will hear a lot more about its home loss to a Milwaukee team that couldn't win on the road until this past weekend than its recent wins over the Spurs, Lakers and Sixers without D-Wade. Something also tells me that the Heatles are used to it by now.

rankings.summaryHtml: They're a win in Sacramento away from a 5-0 road trip and sport the league's third-best record at 30-12 since the Melo trade last February. No wonder Frank Isola of the New York Daily News proclaimed Saturday night on Twitter that we should start calling it the Gallo trade.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Thunder are one of just two teams with a better regular-season record than Denver since Melo was dealt to New York on Feb. 22, 2011: Chicago is 39-7 and OKC is 33-11. But a loss in D.C. -- Durant's hometown! -- isn't easily overlooked by the committee (of one).

rankings.summaryHtml: Villanova-ex Kyle Lowry looks like the early MIP favorite, but Spencer Hawes' growing importance to the Sixers is tangible even when he's not out there. Philly lost by 21 in Miami without its improving center (Achilles) after suffering its first four L's by only 17 points combined.

rankings.summaryHtml: Who had Indy as one of the last two teams, along with Chicago, to be unbeaten at home? Who had the Pacers winning games like Sunday night's in Lakerland when Granger is shooting 35.5 percent? The schedule has been kind, but the truth is they could (and should) be 13-2.

rankings.summaryHtml: Sentences we never thought we'd utter even with Manu still sidelined by that long-term hand injury: San Antonio is tied with its old friends from Lakerland, at 1-6, for the worst road record in the West. No wonder Pop has already publicly blasted the Spurs as "soft."

rankings.summaryHtml: Apologies to the Hawks. They've mostly beaten up on patsies in this 5-1 run without Al Horford, but there's been no dip from them yet. Larry Drew actually called them out for some surrender signs in Friday's loss in Philly ... and they responded by shredding Cleveland by 27.

rankings.summaryHtml: Right there with anything we've seen from a team whose only 2012 losses were inflicted by the Lakers and Mavs by six points combined: Utah just held Kevin Love to 15 and eight. Love's 15 straight double-doubles to start the season was the NBA's longest streak in 30 years.

rankings.summaryHtml: Kobe might be right. Bryant, Pau and Bynum might still be as dangerous as any Big Three. But if there's nothing else behind 'em, this won't work. The case for trading Gasol for a couple of quality youngs, after 11 straight games under 100 points, is only getting stronger.

rankings.summaryHtml: We were prepared to attribute most of the Blazers' struggles since that promising start to the tough schedule they've seen lately. But then they went to Detroit and lost to a team that scores 85 points per game and sports the league's fourth-worst average scoring margin (minus-9.4).

I was already smiling, though, because Brandon Jennings -- PG on our All-Lefty Team -- is playing more efficiently than ever before.

rankings.summaryHtml: The surprise isn't that the reeling Celts are willing to blow up their aging roster. The surprise is that their decision-makers openly acknowledge it, which is going over as well as you'd expect in a locker room you'll recall needed weeks to get over the Perk trade.

rankings.summaryHtml: The compacted season can't go fast enough for the Raps, who are clearly waiting for the draft in June but still have to play 49 games between now and then. They couldn't score with Bargnani and they've lost six in a row without him, posting a high of 91 points in that span.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Bobcats' two best games all season, apart from that thriller they lost at home to Miami in late December, were the two they've played at Madison Square Garden this month. Which makes the slumping Knicks' visit to Charlotte on Monday night unexpectedly crucial viewing.
